# Cost Estimate

## Summary
A card next to the run action that shows what a task will cost before it starts — a figure or range in the product's unit, a rough duration, and a meter of how much of the user's balance it will use. It warns when a run would leave little behind and swaps the action for a top-up when the balance can't cover it.

## When to use
- Usage-priced actions whose cost varies with the input: long documents, batch jobs, video or image generation, agent runs.
- Expensive or slow tasks where an unexpected charge would break trust.
- Settings that change cost (depth, model, length), so users can see the trade-off as they adjust.

## When not to use
- Cheap, everyday actions (a chat reply). Showing a price on every message makes people anxious about using the product.
- Flat-rate plans with no per-action cost. Use Rate Limit when the constraint is a usage cap, not a price.
- When you can't estimate with reasonable accuracy. A wrong estimate is worse than none — show a range or explain what drives cost instead.

## Anatomy
- Estimate: "≈ 26 credits", or a range ("26–33 credits") when cost depends on what the run finds, plus an optional duration.
- Action: the run button, or a "Get more credits" button when the balance is short.
- Balance meter: the remaining balance with the run's share highlighted at the end of it.
- Status line: credits left after the run, a warning when that is low, or how many more credits are needed.
- Optional breakdown: "How is this estimated?" revealing the line items and a note on how billing works.

## Behavior
- The estimate updates live as the user changes inputs; numbers and the meter animate to their new values.
- Warning (amber) when the run would leave less than a set share of the balance; blocked (red) when the upper estimate exceeds the balance, which disables Run or replaces it with a top-up.
- With a range, use the upper bound for warnings, so a run is never started that might be cut off.
- Charge what the run actually uses, and show the final cost afterwards next to the estimate.

## Content guidelines
- Use the product's own unit (credits, tokens, minutes), not money, unless people pay per action in money.
- Round to whole units and prefix single figures with "≈".
- Say what happens at the edges plainly: "Needs 14 more credits than you have", "Leaves you with 8 credits".
- Keep the breakdown to two or three lines in the user's terms ("12 pages × 2 credits"), not internal token counts.

## Accessibility
- The meter is `role="meter"` with a text value ("33 of 120 credits").
- The status line is `aria-live="polite"`, so changes are announced as inputs change, and the Run button is described by it.
- Warning and blocked states use an icon and text as well as colour.
- Animations are skipped when the user prefers reduced motion.

## Related patterns
- Rate Limit is for caps on usage over time; this pattern prices a single action before it runs.
- Model Picker often drives the cost; show the estimate near it when models are priced differently.
- Human-in-the-Loop and Tool Approval are the confirmation step for risky actions; for expensive ones, the estimate is the confirmation.

## Default implementation (Tailwind v4 + Radix + Motion)

This is the catalogue's own reference implementation — use it verbatim when the
host project has no established design system, or when the user asks for
"the demoed look." When the host project has its own design system, treat
this code as a translation reference: keep every rule from the spec above
(Anatomy, Behavior, Content guidelines, Accessibility) and re-express the
markup, styling, and motion using that system's own components/tokens
instead of copying these Tailwind classes or the Motion API.

```tsx
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import { AnimatePresence, motion, useReducedMotion, useSpring, useTransform } from "motion/react";
import { ChevronDown, TriangleAlert } from "lucide-react";

import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

export interface CostLine {
  label: string;
  amount: number;
}

export interface CostEstimateProps {
  /** Expected cost. Pass `max` too when the cost can only be given as a range. */
  min: number;
  max?: number;
  /** What the user has left. */
  balance: number;
  /** Unit name in the plural ("credits", "tokens"). */
  unit?: string;
  /** Rough duration, already formatted ("~2 min"). */
  duration?: string;
  /** What the estimate is made of; shown behind "How is this estimated?". */
  breakdown?: CostLine[];
  /** Warn when what's left after the run would fall below this share of the balance. */
  warnBelow?: number;
  actionLabel?: string;
  onRun?: () => void;
  topUpLabel?: string;
  onTopUp?: () => void;
  className?: string;
}

type Level = "ok" | "warn" | "blocked";

export function CostEstimate({
  min,
  max,
  balance,
  unit = "credits",
  duration,
  breakdown,
  warnBelow = 0.2,
  actionLabel = "Run",
  onRun,
  topUpLabel = "Get more credits",
  onTopUp,
  className,
}: CostEstimateProps) {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();
  const id = React.useId();

  const high = Math.max(min, max ?? min);
  const after = Math.max(0, balance - high);
  const level: Level = high > balance ? "blocked" : after < balance * warnBelow ? "warn" : "ok";
  const range = max !== undefined && max !== min;

  const total = Math.max(balance, 1);
  const usedPct = Math.min(100, (Math.min(high, balance) / total) * 100);

  return (
    <div className={cn("flex w-full flex-col gap-3 rounded-2xl border bg-card p-4", className)}>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-4 gap-y-3">
        <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
          <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Estimated cost</p>
          <p className="mt-0.5 text-lg font-semibold tabular-nums">
            {range ? (
              <>
                <AnimatedNumber value={min} instant={!!reduceMotion} />–<AnimatedNumber value={high} instant={!!reduceMotion} />
              </>
            ) : (
              <>
                ≈ <AnimatedNumber value={min} instant={!!reduceMotion} />
              </>
            )}{" "}
            <span className="text-sm font-normal text-muted-foreground">{unit}</span>
            {duration && <span className="text-sm font-normal text-muted-foreground"> · {duration}</span>}
          </p>
        </div>

        {level === "blocked" && onTopUp ? (
          <button
            type="button"
            onClick={onTopUp}
            className="shrink-0 rounded-xl bg-foreground px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-background transition-opacity hover:opacity-90"
          >
            {topUpLabel}
          </button>
        ) : (
          <button
            type="button"
            onClick={onRun}
            disabled={level === "blocked"}
            aria-describedby={`${id}-status`}
            className="shrink-0 rounded-xl bg-foreground px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-background transition-opacity hover:opacity-90 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-40"
          >
            {actionLabel}
          </button>
        )}
      </div>

      <div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
        <div
          role="meter"
          aria-label={`Share of balance this run uses`}
          aria-valuemin={0}
          aria-valuemax={balance}
          aria-valuenow={Math.min(high, balance)}
          aria-valuetext={`${high} of ${balance} ${unit}`}
          className="relative h-2 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-muted"
        >
          <motion.div
            className="absolute inset-y-0 left-0 rounded-full bg-muted-foreground/30"
            initial={false}
            animate={{ width: `${100 - usedPct}%` }}
            transition={reduceMotion ? { duration: 0 } : { type: "spring", stiffness: 180, damping: 26 }}
          />
          <motion.div
            className={cn(
              "absolute inset-y-0 rounded-full",
              level === "ok" && "bg-foreground",
              level === "warn" && "bg-amber-500",
              level === "blocked" && "bg-destructive"
            )}
            initial={false}
            animate={{ left: `${100 - usedPct}%`, width: `${usedPct}%` }}
            transition={reduceMotion ? { duration: 0 } : { type: "spring", stiffness: 180, damping: 26 }}
          />
        </div>

        <div id={`${id}-status`} aria-live="polite" className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-x-3 gap-y-1 text-xs">
          {level === "blocked" ? (
            <span className="flex items-center gap-1 font-medium text-destructive">
              <TriangleAlert className="size-3.5" aria-hidden />
              Needs {high - balance} more {unit} than you have
            </span>
          ) : level === "warn" ? (
            <span className="flex items-center gap-1 font-medium text-amber-700 dark:text-amber-400">
              <TriangleAlert className="size-3.5" aria-hidden />
              Leaves you with {after} {unit}
            </span>
          ) : (
            <span className="text-muted-foreground">
              {after} {unit} left after this run
            </span>
          )}
          <span className="text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">
            Balance {balance} {unit}
          </span>
        </div>
      </div>

      {breakdown && breakdown.length > 0 && (
        <div className="border-t pt-2">
          <button
            type="button"
            aria-expanded={open}
            aria-controls={`${id}-breakdown`}
            onClick={() => setOpen((o) => !o)}
            className="flex items-center gap-1 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground transition-colors hover:text-foreground"
          >
            How is this estimated?
            <ChevronDown className={cn("size-3.5 transition-transform", open && "rotate-180")} aria-hidden />
          </button>
          <AnimatePresence initial={false}>
            {open && (
              <motion.div
                id={`${id}-breakdown`}
                initial={{ height: 0, opacity: 0 }}
                animate={{ height: "auto", opacity: 1 }}
                exit={{ height: 0, opacity: 0 }}
                transition={{ duration: 0.18, ease: "easeOut" }}
                className="overflow-hidden"
              >
                <dl className="mt-2 flex flex-col gap-1 text-xs">
                  {breakdown.map((line) => (
                    <div key={line.label} className="flex justify-between gap-3">
                      <dt className="text-muted-foreground">{line.label}</dt>
                      <dd className="tabular-nums">
                        {line.amount} {unit}
                      </dd>
                    </div>
                  ))}
                </dl>
                <p className="mt-2 text-xs text-pretty text-muted-foreground">
                  You&apos;re only charged for what the run actually uses.
                </p>
              </motion.div>
            )}
          </AnimatePresence>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

function AnimatedNumber({ value, instant }: { value: number; instant: boolean }) {
  const spring = useSpring(value, { stiffness: 220, damping: 30 });
  const rounded = useTransform(spring, (v) => Math.round(v).toLocaleString());

  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (instant) spring.jump(value);
    else spring.set(value);
  }, [spring, value, instant]);

  return <motion.span>{rounded}</motion.span>;
}
```
